definition: Forecasting traffic flow, speed, or congestion from sensor and historical data, typically with spatiotemporal GNNs.
details: Forecasting traffic flow, speed, or congestion from sensor and historical data, typically with spatiotemporal GNNs.

explainer.lead: Traffic prediction forecasts flow, speed, or congestion ahead of time so networks can be managed proactively rather than reacted to. It matters because accurate forecasts support routing, signal timing, and incident response.

tiers.eli5: It's like guessing how busy a road will be later, the way you predict the supermarket gets crowded at 6pm.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers feed sensor readings and historical patterns into spatiotemporal GNNs that model both space (neighbouring roads) and time. A common pitfall is that traffic regimes shift with incidents or weather, so models trained on normal days degrade when conditions change.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, given sensor observations over a road graph G and past time steps, the model learns a mapping to future flow or speed values per node or edge; spatiotemporal GNNs combine graph convolution across roads with temporal layers across time. Limits include sensitivity to sensor outages and to non-recurring events not in the training data.

explainer.example: Using loop-detector counts from the past hour across a city grid, a spatiotemporal GNN predicts the next 15 minutes of flow on each road segment.
